statements.text: America should be the world’s innovation leader — but it shouldn’t come at the cost of our children’s safety, our workers’ livelihoods, or the reliability of the news we consume. [...] And while we want to protect America’s leadership in artificial intelligence, we are still grappling with how it will affect everything from how we work to how our children learn. We must protect Americans and establish clear, consistent laws for businesses.
statements.venue: Campaign website, issues page on social media, AI and tech

statements.text: And we can establish an AI dividend, so every American citizen owns a piece of these American AI companies. If they are going to use our human ingenuity and our collective intellectual property, then we want our royalty checks.
statements.venue: Campaign speech video on AI dividend

statements.text: We are about to fall off the cliff
statements.venue: Plano town hall, as reported by Dallas Observer (on unregulated AI)

statements.text: No. In the Legislature, we established the AI Advisory Council to create guidelines for the responsible use of AI in state agencies — and these policies shouldn’t be preempted. In the Senate, I will support safeguards to keep kids safe online, like prohibiting platforms from using algorithms to send targeted content to minors and reining in social media’s broad immunity protections. I’ll champion legislation to protect workers from invasive AI surveillance in the workplace, use AI to make jobs safer and less repetitive instead of replacing them, and create pathways for workers to move into better-paying jobs as the economy evolves.
statements.venue: Texas Tribune Q&A with Democratic Senate candidates (answer on federal preemption of state AI regulation)

statements.text: Texas should be a leader when it comes to innovation and technology, but that only works if Texans get a say and get a share of that economic growth — and that’s not what’s happening right now. [...] We’re often told in our politics that we have to choose between policies that are pro-growth and pro-people. I reject that choice, and the plan that we’re outlining today to hold data centers accountable, I think, strikes a balance between welcoming those investments while also protecting working people.
statements.venue: News conference in Austin rolling out data center plan

statements.text: We cannot let artificial intelligence become yet another arena where billionaires write the rules for the rest of us. Working people must get a say — and a share — in that AI future.
statements.venue: Campaign speech on 'AI Dividend', as reported by Nexstar/KTAL

statements.text: When you look at this ad, they are using AI in order to mislead the people of this state, and that is completely consistent with a liar like Ken Paxton
statements.venue: CBS News interview with Ed O'Keefe on Paxton's AI-generated ad

statements.text:
Have y’all seen these AI deepfakes they’re making of me?
